scope: Shared cross-owner pass identity versus owner-local native command proof

findings.status: source-confirmed structural gap; physical impact unverified
findings.path: DrivingPassContext actor receipt captures currentCommand and expectedDestination for every actor without locality filtering. Proposing owner supplies both rows. Server topology deliberately compares fields0..6,9,10 and omits command/destination7,8; actual owner later compares entire row against proposing observer row. DrivingPassBegin and geometry/traffic preparation compare whole context; DrivingPassStep compares peerRow through the same observer reader.
findings.impact: Shared native destination is not independent current-owner evidence. Different observer results can refuse valid cross-owner consent or interpret peer changes from the wrong machine. Do not claim every cross-owner pass fails without a fresh physical trace.
findings.comparison: DrivingQueueContext explicitly leaves shared destination slot empty; actual owner captures private ownerOrders. That is the existing architectural reference, not permission to weaken pass checks.

required_implementation: Use canonical shared authored route/seat/owner/epoch/generation identity independent of observer-native destination. Preserve schema consumers deliberately; do not merely blank the field.

Capture each consenting vehicle original native commands/destinations privately on its actual owner before ACK, bind full token/serial/context/original expiry, and compare that proof through RESULT/admission. Root preparation must retain local pre-command cancellation proof.

Maintain peer-owner consent revocation when its native task changes during the pass; root cannot replace this with remote expectedDestination. Trace existing driving callback for bounded revocation before adding a new worker. Root execution and return must retain their existing exact local journals.

Retire companion proof with exact token/epoch/generation, terminal result, original expiry, locality loss and shutdown without deleting successor proof. Preserve duplicate phases, token closure, broker callback bounds and all native-MOVE exclusions until separately implemented.
